body: You could move this note to the description of STRETCH_TILE.

Actually, this is bad, it warns only once for the whole lifetime of the project/editor. Meaning after creating such wrong setup (`STRETCH_TILE` + `AtlasTexture` with non-zero `margin`) in the editor once, you won't be warned again if you'd again create similar wrong setup e.g. in different TextureRect (not until you'd restart the editor).

I could change it to `WARN_PRINT`, but then it could spam the warning for such wrong setup (seems to be doing so e.g. on dragging given TextureRect within the editor). But that's probably fine? 🤔 Such setup would not work correctly, hence should be fixed by the user (and doing so would get rid of the potential warning spam).

Alternative I guess would be to show this in the node configuration warning, but this would be only shown in the editor (so no warning for stuff created dynamically on runtime). +It would require connecting to `AtlasTexture.changed` signal for properly updating. Seems like unnecessary overhead for such a niche case to me. So I think `WARN_PRINT` is probably the way to go.

@KoBeWi What do you think?
